# Chip

> A read-only label pill in the mono label type: a skill, a tag, a role.

Part of the [Nate Mills Design System](../README.md). It is a CSS class API, not a JavaScript component, so its props are the classes and HTML attributes below. Link the stylesheets as [Getting started](../foundations/getting-started.md) shows, then add the classes. Every component: [Components](../COMPONENTS.md).

## When to use

- A label or a tag that describes something: a skill, a discipline, a role.

## When not to use

- A status, such as "Open to work": use a Badge.
- A position in a carousel: use the Carousel navigation counter.
- Anything clickable: use a Button or a Link.

## Alternatives

- **[Badge](badge.md):** Same pill shape, different job: a chip labels, a badge reports a status. Pick by what the words do.
- **[Button](button.md):** A chip never takes a click. If a tag has to act, it is a Button.
- **[Section heading](section-heading.md):** A section label names a part of the page; a chip labels a thing inside it.

## How to use

**Element:** `<span>`

- Put `.chip` on a `<span>` with the label as its text.
- Add `.chip--outline` where the filled chip carries too much weight.
- A leading Lucide glyph is optional; mark it `aria-hidden="true"`.

**Classes:** `.chip`, `.chip--outline`

## Props

| Prop | Type | Allowed values | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | modifier class | `outline` (`.chip--outline`) | No class: a sunken fill. | How much weight the chip carries. |
| `icon` | child element | A leading Lucide `<i data-lucide="..." aria-hidden="true">` | None. | Optional. Sized by the chip; always `aria-hidden`, so the word carries the meaning. |

## Variants

Available variants: `outline`.

- `outline` (`.chip--outline`): The fill drops out, for quieter contexts.

Default variant: No class: a sunken fill.

## States

No interactive states: a chip is a label and never takes a click or focus.

## Invalid combinations

Options that must not be used together. Each names the props above.

| Combination | Level | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `.chip` on a `<button>` or an `<a>` | MUST NOT | A chip is a label, with no focus or pressed state. |
| `.chip` with a status word, such as "Open to work" | MUST NOT | A status is a Badge. |
| `icon` with no `aria-hidden="true"` | MUST NOT | The word carries the meaning; a screen reader should not read the glyph. |

## Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Passes over it: a chip is not focusable. |
| Enter, Space | Do nothing: a chip takes no input. |
| Down arrow in a screen reader's browse mode (VoiceOver: VO + Right arrow) | Reads the label word. A leading glyph is `aria-hidden`, so it is skipped. |

A chip is a label; if it must act, use a Button.

## Rules

| Level | Rule | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| MUST NOT | Make a `.chip` interactive. | [Automated: Component-rules lint](../foundations/checks.md#component-rules-lint) |
| MUST | Mark a leading glyph `aria-hidden="true"`. | [Automated: Component-rules lint](../foundations/checks.md#component-rules-lint) |
| MUST NOT | Report a status on a chip. | [Manual: Label-or-status review](../foundations/checks.md#label-or-status-review) |

Automated checks run on natemills.me before every publish; the scripts live in the private source repository.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use `.chip` for a label; a status or a count belongs on `.badge` instead.
- Keep a chip a plain `span`; a tag that has to act becomes a `button`, not a clickable label.
- Reach for `.chip--outline` in quieter contexts where the sunken fill carries too much weight.
- Mark a leading glyph `aria-hidden` so the word carries the meaning and the icon stays decoration.

### Don't

- Do not give `.chip` a focus or pressed state; it is a label, and a press precedent promises behaviour it has none of.
- Do not report status on a chip; `.badge` owns status and count, and the split is what keeps both readable.
- Do not change `.chip` off `--font-feature-mono`; `font-feature-settings` replaces rather than merges, so the slashed zero dies.
- Do not size a chip glyph by hand; `--chip-icon-size` normalises Lucide strokes and brand marks to one footprint.

## Example

```html
<span class="chip chip--outline">Design systems</span>
```

## Look

- **Chips vs badges vs counters** resolve by job: a label is a chip, a status is a badge, a count is
  the carousel counter. A badge is read-only and never interactive; its dot stays lime in both themes
  but colour is never the only signal, every status also carries a word.

Values in braces, such as `{colors.border}`, are named on the foundation pages, starting with [Colour](../foundations/color.md); every token with its purpose is on [Tokens](../foundations/tokens.md).

## Recipe

The recipe from [DESIGN.md](../DESIGN.md), one entry per state. Names in braces resolve on the foundation pages.

```yaml
chip:
  backgroundColor: "{colors.surface-sunken}"
  textColor: "{colors.text-primary}"
  border: "{structure.border-hairline}"
  typography: "{typography.label} mono, weight 500"
  rounded: "{rounded.full}"
  padding: "4px 10px"
```

## Classes

| Class | Kind | What it does | Tokens it reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.chip` | base | sunken fill, mono label | `--chip-bg`, `--chip-border`, `--chip-fg`, `--chip-font`, `--chip-font-size`, `--chip-font-weight`, `--chip-gap`, `--chip-line`, `--chip-pad-x`, `--chip-pad-y`, `--chip-radius`, `--font-feature-mono` |
| `.chip--outline` | modifier | fill drops out for quieter contexts | `--color-text-secondary` |

## Tokens

Every token the classes above read, as data from tokens.json: write `var(--name)`, never the raw value. A component token belongs to one component: change it to restyle that component and nothing else. A semantic token is a shared role; never change one for a single component. The three tiers: [Tokens](../foundations/tokens.md#three-tiers).

| Token | Tier | Value | What it is for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--chip-bg` | Component | `#ececec`; dark `#141416`, from `--color-surface-sunken` | Chip fill at rest (and on active). |
| `--chip-border` | Component | `#e4e4e7`; dark `#27272a`, from `--color-border` | Chip border at rest. |
| `--chip-fg` | Component | `#0a0a0b`; dark `#f4f4f5`, from `--color-text-primary` | Chip label and icon colour. |
| `--chip-font` | Component | `"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`, from `--font-mono` | Chip label typeface (JetBrains Mono). |
| `--chip-font-size` | Component | `0.6875rem`, from `--text-label` | Chip label size. |
| `--chip-font-weight` | Component | `500`, from `--weight-medium` | Chip label weight. |
| `--chip-gap` | Component | `8px`, from `--space-200` | Space between a chip's icon and its label. |
| `--chip-line` | Component | `1.4` | Chip label line height. Component-level literal, sized to the mono label; off the named line scale by design. |
| `--chip-pad-x` | Component | `10px` | Chip inline (left/right) padding. Component-level literal; sits off the 4px space scale by design (between space-200 and space-300), kept so the live chip is unchanged. |
| `--chip-pad-y` | Component | `4px`, from `--space-100` | Chip block (top/bottom) padding; 4px. |
| `--chip-radius` | Component | `999px`, from `--radius-full` | Chip corner radius; full pill. |
| `--color-text-secondary` | Semantic | `#3f3f46`; dark `#a1a1aa`, from `--neutral-700` | Secondary text: supporting copy one step quieter than text-primary. Checked at 4.5:1 on bg, surface, surface-sunken and the four tint surfaces; for labels and quiet meta copy use text-tertiary. |
| `--font-feature-mono` | Semantic | `"zero" 1` | Switches on the slashed zero for every piece of mono text. |
